findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the filled 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's main action does nothing. The filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address next to it look clickable, but the parts map lists both as static (p11–p13). A click opens no email. The only working email link is in the footer, at the very end of a long page.
findings.who_objects: The development-bank official who has decided to contact Mark. They click 'Write to me' or the address, nothing happens, and an advisor's site that can't take an enquiry looks careless or abandoned.

findings.where: First screen, 'Book a consultation', the second filled blue button (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: There are two primary actions of equal weight where the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark. The second offers a booking service the brief never mentions. Its link goes to #consult, and no booking or consultation section appears anywhere on the page, so the click goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who has to choose between two identical blue buttons and then finds the booking one goes nowhere. The founder, whose rule is one action and one personal route. 'Book a consultation' also reads like a firm's sales funnel, not a personal advisor.

findings.where: First screen, the hero ground: a pale blue-to-lilac-pink gradient behind the whole hero (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pastel lavender gradient that is not in the house palette. The page's own palette section says 'three colours, no accent' with a warm paper ground (#F7F5EE), and the rest of the page uses that paper. The brief asks for one soft, warm paper ground with blue and grey as the only ink. The gradient brings in a pink-violet hue and the look of a tech start-up.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark: the brief bans a slick look and anything 'in-your-face techy'. A multilateral-bank official reads a lilac gradient as a software product's landing page, not a legal advisor's brief. The hero also clashes with the paper of every section below it.

findings.where: Margin notes beside the hero (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024 with their talk titles). The same blue static labels recur on every specimen section (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes) and on the blue 'MMM INFRA' type sample
findings.fault: The margin notes are set in the house blue, which the page uses for its links and buttons, and they name real talks. But they are static (p5–p10), so blue no longer means 'clickable'. A visitor who clicks 'Best Practices in PPP Legislation for Emerging Economies' to read the talk gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: The official, who wants evidence of relevant work and tries to open the talk the note names. They hit dead text and lose the proof the note was meant to give. The brief specifies blue margin notes, so this clash between the brief's look and the link colour goes to the founder.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person intro paragraph 'I advise multilateral development banks…' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The one sentence that says what Mark does and for whom is set as four lines of widely spaced bold capitals (eight on phone). It is the hardest-to-read style on the page, and it turns a personal sentence into a shouted corporate label.
findings.who_objects: The visitor doing the five-second test, who needs exactly this sentence and has to work through it letter by letter. Mark, whose quiet first-person voice reads here as a banner.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the order of heading, photo, intro, notes and contact row
findings.fault: At phone width the photo and the three margin notes sit between the paragraphs, so the intro is broken up by blue notes. The contact row only arrives about three screens down. In that row 'Book a consultation' is indented away from the left edge that 'Write to me' and the address share, and it sits right under the address, so the group looks loosely stacked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone, who opens the site from a LinkedIn link, has to scroll through notes that interrupt the text to find how to reach Mark, and then finds a contact block that looks misaligned.

findings.fault: Apart from the three talk titles, the hero gives no proof that Mark has done this work for bodies like theirs. No named body asked for his work, there are no work rows and no newest article with a working link. The only checkable items, the talks, are not links.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who hires through procurement against terms of reference and needs checkable specifics: which banks or governments, which countries. Without them the hero rests on a heading and an adjective-free but unproven claim.

findings.where: Motion section: the exhibit photo with its 'Replay the entrance' table, on the right of the desktop layout
findings.fault: The sample photo hangs low on the far right, below the level of the curve, and splits across two screens. A large empty area sits under the curve on the left, so the section looks unbalanced and its parts don't read as one group.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the motion sketch: the thing that moves is pushed to the edge, away from the curve that describes it.

findings.where: Motion section, the display line 'Placed. Settled. Still.'
findings.fault: A three-word slogan set in large display type reads as an advertising tagline.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brief bars a corporate tagline and anything cheesy or salesy, and this line is decoration in Mark's display voice that he never said.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' button on the PDF row, against the hero buttons
findings.fault: The page has two button shapes: square filled buttons in the hero and a rounded outlined pill for Download. Nothing explains why the two actions look different.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add more PDF rows and buttons and has no single button style to follow. Careful readers see a site that looks put together from different kits.
